title: Search shows results for the previous keystroke
why: Typing 'tea' shows the right result for a split second, then the results for 'te' replace it. Whether it happens depends on network timing, so it's flaky by nature.
html:
Typing 'tea' shows the right result for a split second, then the results for 'te' replace it. Whether it happens depends on network timing, so it's flaky by nature.

What the recording showed. Each keystroke sends its own /api/search request. The response for q=te arrived after the one for q=tea and overwrote it. The server returned 1 match for 'tea'; the list showed 4, including 'Write blog post'.

Moment What happened
type 't','e','a' 3 requests in flight
tea → 200 1 correct result rendered
te → 200 (late) overwrites the list

Open in Replay QA · Open Replay recording

Loading session replay…

Journey: Detail: Search matches case-insensitively, on partial and multi-word queries, and shows no results for non-matches · Found 2026-06-12

Description

The Search view fires one /api/search request per keystroke but does not guard against out-of-order responses. When typing 'tea', the response for the earlier query 'te' arrives after the response for 'tea' and overwrites it, so the input shows 'tea' while the list shows the 4 results for 'te' — including 'Write blog post', 'Update onboarding docs' and 'Prepare investor update', none of which contain 'tea' in their name. The server itself returns only 1 task ('Plan team offsite') for q=tea, so the displayed list is plainly wrong.

Actual behavior

The input shows 'tea' but the list shows '4 results' — the results for the earlier query 'te' (Plan team offsite, Update onboarding docs, Write blog post, Prepare investor update). The correct 'tea' result (1 task) is briefly shown and then replaced by the late-arriving 'te' response. 'Write blog post', which contains no 'tea', remains visible.

Expected behavior

After the input settles on 'tea', the list should show only the result(s) for 'tea'. The server returns exactly one task for /api/search?q=tea ('Plan team offsite'), so only that task should be displayed; non-matching tasks like 'Write blog post' should not appear.

Root cause

The Search view runs a useEffect keyed only on the query string that, for every change, issues GET /api/search?q=<query> and unconditionally writes the response into result state — useEffect(()=>{let t=e.trim();if(!t){r([]);return}a(!0),Or.search(t).then(e=>{r(e.results),a(!1)})},[e]), where search:e=>Dr(/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(e)}). The effect uses no AbortController and performs no check that the resolving response belongs to the current query, so the result state is set by whichever request resolves last rather than the most recent query. Because each keystroke starts its own request and the requests have varying durations, an earlier request can resolve after a later one and overwrite the correct results. For 'tea', /api/search?q=tea resolved at 31515ms but the earlier /api/search?q=te resolved later at 31712ms, so the stale 'te' results (4 tasks) replaced the correct 'tea' result (1 task) and remained on screen.

title: Checkout charges the pre-discount total after a promo code
why: The button says Pay $117.00 and the order goes through. Only the amount charged is wrong, and only when the promo is applied after the checkout page has loaded.
html:
The button says Pay $117.00 and the order goes through. Only the amount charged is wrong, and only when the promo is applied after the checkout page has loaded.

What the recording showed. placeOrder is memoized with useCallback(…, [cart?.id]), so it kept the total from before the promo. POST /api/orders sent amount: 130 while the button read Pay $117.00, and order #10422 was charged $130.00.

Moment What happened
apply WELCOME10 total re-renders to $117
click Pay $117.00 POST amount: 130
confirmation Total charged $130.00

Open in Replay QA · Open Replay recording

Session replay

Loading session replay…

Journey: Complete purchase: browse the catalog, add items to the cart, and check out with a promo code · Found 2026-10-20

Description

On the Hearth & Field checkout page, applying promo code WELCOME10 (10% off, verified via /api/promo returning {"code":"WELCOME10","percent":10}) correctly re-renders the summary to Subtotal $130.00 / Discount (WELCOME10) -$13.00 / Total $117.00 and the pay button to "Pay $117.00". But clicking Pay posts amount:130 (the undiscounted subtotal) to POST /api/orders, so the created order #10422 is stored and its confirmation page shows "Total charged $130.00" with no discount — the customer is charged the full pre-discount price. The stale $130 is sent because the placeOrder submit handler is memoized with useCallback(..., [cart?.id]) and closes over the pre-discount total.

Actual behavior

The POST /api/orders request body sends "amount":130 even though the pay button just read "Pay $117.00"; the server creates order #10422 with amount 130, and the order confirmation page displays "Total charged $130.00" with no discount amount shown — the applied WELCOME10 promo is silently dropped from the charged total.

Expected behavior

After applying WELCOME10 and seeing Total $117.00 / "Pay $117.00", placing the order should submit amount 117, and the order confirmation for Order #10422 should show the discounted total charged (e.g. $117.00 with the -$13.00 discount reflected), matching what the shopper agreed to pay at checkout.

Root cause

In src/pages/Checkout.jsx, the order submit handler placeOrder is created with useCallback(..., [cart?.id]) and posts amount: total (line 56) from its closure. total is derived as round2(subtotal - discount + shipping) (line 34) where discount = subtotal * promo.percent / 100 (line 32). When the WELCOME10 promo is applied, setPromo re-renders and total falls from 130 to 117, but because the only dependency cart?.id is unchanged, React keeps the previously memoized handler which still closes over the old total = 130. Clicking 'Pay $117.00' therefore executes the stale closure and sends amount:130 to POST /api/orders (verified: request body {"cartId":"1335c46e-06eb-495c-8e0e-9392c5d6dee8","amount":130,...} at 164639ms, after the promo was applied at ~150000ms), so the placed order records the full undiscounted charge.

title: Home greeting fails hydration: ‘Good afternoon’ vs ‘Good evening’
why: React regenerates the tree on the client, so the page ends up looking right. The mismatch only exists between the server HTML and the first client render.
html:
React regenerates the tree on the client, so the page ends up looking right. The mismatch only exists between the server HTML and the first client render.

What the recording showed. Greeting.tsx creates new Date() in a useState initializer on both sides. The server rendered an afternoon hour and ‘Good afternoon’; the client rendered 8:55 PM and ‘Good evening’, so React threw #418.

Session replay

Journey: Browse projects from the home dashboard · Found 2026-10-19

Description

On initial load of the homepage (team-portal, path "/"), the server-rendered <h1> inside the hero card says "Good afternoon, Dana", but the client's first render computes "Good evening, Dana" from the user's local time (8:55 PM). React 18/19 hydration detects the text mismatch, logs React error #418 ("Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client"), and discards/regenerates the entire server-rendered tree on the client. Trigger: loading the page at any time where the server's hour bucket (hour < 12 / < 18 / else) differs from the browser's local hour bucket — e.g. evenings for a server running in a different timezone. Impact: a visible greeting flash/wrong greeting on first paint plus a full client re-render of the page instead of hydration, with the error logged to console on every such load.

Actual behavior

React error #418: Hydration failed. This error causes visual inconsistencies — the UI may not match what the server rendered Hydration failed. First occurrence: "Uncaught Error: Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client. As a result this tree will be regenerated on the client. This can happen if a SSR-ed Client Component used: -…". Suggested action: The server-rendered HTML doesn't match what the client renders. Common cause: using browser-only values (Date.now(), window.*) during SSR.

Expected behavior

The server-rendered HTML and the client's first (hydration) render should produce identical text — the hero <h1> should read the same greeting (e.g. "Good evening, Dana") during hydration, with no React error #418 and no regeneration of the server tree. Time-dependent text should be rendered deterministically (e.g. computed only after mount via useEffect, or initialized from a timestamp passed from the server).

Root cause

components/Greeting.tsx initializes time-dependent state with a fresh Date on both server and client: line 12 const [now, setNow] = useState(() => new Date()), and the render at line 22 calls greetingFor(now.getHours()). The server rendered the page when now.getHours() fell in the 12–17 bucket, so greetingFor returned "Good afternoon"; the client's first render created a different Date (local time 8:55 PM, hour 20), so greetingFor returned "Good evening". The two text nodes for the same <h1> differ, hydration fails with React error #418, and React throws away the server tree and regenerates it on the client (onRecoverableError → recoverable hydration error).

Description

On a project's Settings tab, the Team Members section lets an owner invite a new member by email. After typing a valid email (newmember@example.com) and clicking Invite, the invite fails: a runtime TypeError 'Cannot add property 2, object is not extensible' is surfaced (shown in a role=alert error and carried by the rejected Redux thunk), and the new member is NOT added to the team list. Actual behavior

The invite thunk throws a TypeError 'Cannot add property 2, object is not extensible' (projectMembers/invite/rejected). No member is added — the list still shows only dev@example.local (Owner) and collaborator@example.com (Member), and newmember@example.com remains in the input field.

Expected behavior

Clicking Invite with a valid email should add the new member to the Team Members list as a 'Member' (e.g. newmember@example.com shown with a Member badge) and clear the input field.

Root cause

In src/dev/mockPipeline.ts, mockInviteMember reads the project's member array with const list = store.membersByProject[projectId] ?? [] and then calls list.push(m) (mockPipeline.ts:1365-1366). Redux Toolkit (Immer) freezes state in development, so once that array was placed in the store it became non-extensible. Calling Array.push on the now-frozen array throws 'TypeError: Cannot add property 2, object is not extensible' (the existing array already holds 2 members at indices 0 and 1, so adding index 2 fails). Journey: Paginate the accounts table and change rows per page · Found 2026-10-19

Description

Every grid row renders an OwnerCell (src/components/OwnerCell.jsx) that fires its own fetchUser(ownerId) in a useEffect on mount. All 50 rows share ownerId 23, so 11 identical GET requests to /api/users/23 are issued — 7 of them within a 99ms burst at load (1576–1675ms), each taking 0.5–9.3 seconds and occupying a server connection. The user-visible effect is that owner names/avatars across the grid sit in the 'owner-loading' skeleton state far longer than necessary while these redundant in-flight requests contend with the grid's own data fetches (205 of the recording's 311 requests were ≥2s). The app even ships an unused batch endpoint fetchUsers(ids) (src/lib/api.js line 28) that would fetch all owners in one call.

Actual behavior

11 identical GET requests to /api/users/23 are issued: 7 in a burst at initial load (1576ms, 1578ms, 1602ms, 1624ms, 1635ms, 1645ms, 1675ms — all 200, durations 1133ms to 9310ms), 2 more after the first row click at 121264ms/121288ms, and 2 more after the second click at 167697ms/167699ms. Each OwnerCell mounts its own fetch and the results are never shared, so the same user record is transferred and processed repeatedly.

Expected behavior

The owner for ownerId 23 should be fetched once (deduplicated across the 50 OwnerCell instances, or fetched for all rows in a single batched call via the existing fetchUsers(ids) endpoint) and reused from a shared cache/state; owner names should appear after one request round-trip.

Root cause

src/components/OwnerCell.jsx issues fetchUser(ownerId) inside a useEffect that runs on every component mount (line 9), and src/state/columns.jsx line 97 renders one <OwnerCell ownerId={r.ownerId}/> per grid row. With 50 rows all referencing ownerId 23, every mounting row independently requests the same /api/users/23 endpoint — 11 mounts fired during the recording — with no deduplication, shared cache, or use of the existing batch endpoint fetchUsers(ids) in src/lib/api.js (line 28). Confirmed by the network log: 11 GETs to /api/users/23, all 200, including 7 within 99ms at load with durations 1133–9310ms.
